rules.title: Exactly one primary action per screen
rules.description: Each screen exposes exactly one primary-variant action so the user's next step is unambiguous. Supporting actions use the secondary variant.

rules.title: Action labels state the action
rules.description: Button labels describe what happens ('Create account', 'Place order'). Generic labels such as 'Submit', 'OK' or 'Yes' are forbidden.

rules.title: Destructive actions require confirmation
rules.description: Hard-to-reverse actions (delete account, cancel subscription) never execute directly; they open a confirmation dialog first.

rules.title: Destructive confirmations state the consequence
rules.description: A destructive confirmation dialog states the irreversible consequence in body text, uses a danger-variant confirm button whose label repeats the action, and offers a safe cancel.

rules.title: Destructive controls live in a separated danger zone
rules.description: Destructive controls are grouped in their own clearly titled card, never adjacent to routine save actions.

rules.title: Every field has a visible label
rules.description: Every form field has a non-empty, programmatically associated visible label. Placeholders never substitute for labels.

rules.title: Personal-data fields declare autocomplete
rules.description: Fields collecting information about the user (name, email, address, payment card) declare the matching HTML autocomplete purpose.

rules.title: Focus indicators are never suppressed
rules.description: All interactive elements show a visible focus ring using the color.border.focus token. Styles that remove outlines are forbidden.

rules.title: Every error state offers recovery
rules.description: Every error message is actionable, preserves user input, and tells the user what to do next. Dead-end errors are forbidden.

rules.title: Errors are textual and announced
rules.description: Validation errors render as text adjacent to the offending field and are announced to assistive technology (role=alert); color alone never signals an error.

rules.title: Layouts collapse below the md breakpoint
rules.description: Multi-column layouts collapse to a single column below breakpoint.md (768px). Forms are single-column at every width.

rules.title: Full cost is visible at the point of commitment
rules.description: Any screen with a paying/committing action shows the complete cost breakdown (including taxes and fees) as a summary on the same screen.

rules.title: The committing label carries the consequence
rules.description: The button that commits a payment or contract states the amount or consequence in its label ('Place order and pay 62.90 EUR').

rules.title: Recurring charges disclose renewal terms
rules.description: Before committing to a recurring charge, the summary states the cadence and that it renews until cancelled.

rules.title: First contact asks for the minimum
rules.description: The first screen of an acquisition or recovery flow asks for at most three fields; everything else is deferred.

rules.title: Optional steps are skippable
rules.description: A step that collects only optional data offers an explicit secondary 'Skip for now' action.

rules.title: Never disclose account existence
rules.description: Account-recovery responses are identical whether or not the address is registered ('If an account exists, we sent a link').

rules.title: Sensitive values never reach logs
rules.description: Payment and credential fields are marked sensitive; their values are never persisted in audit logs or traces - only field names are.

rules.title: Defer everything but credentials at signup
rules.description: Signup collects credentials only; profile and preference data is collected after the user has reached first value, and is optional.

rules.title: Checkout failures preserve everything
rules.description: When payment or address validation fails, all entered data is kept and the user is returned to the failing step with the offending field focused.
